title: Daily activity and visual discrimination reflects the eye organization of weaver ant Oecophylla smaragdina (Insecta: Hymenoptera: Formicidae)
why: Oecophylla smaragdina: sweep-26 opened this preprint and records that it gives the interommatidial angle of the weaver ant's compound eye in its Figure 4E only (its text gives 710 to 790 facets and lens diameters of 13 to 18 µm), so a reader of the figure could log interommatidial_deg for the species. Ogawa et al. 2023 (10.1007/s00359-023-01629-7), which main read in full (oa-5), states no interommatidial angle in its text. Returned by the harvest queries "Oecophylla vision", "Oecophylla eye" and "Oecophylla visual acuity" and by both web searches for visual acuity; not opened in this unit.

Rusa unicolor: an open-access Folia Morphologica article ranked first (journals.viamedica.pl) and second (as https://dx.doi.org/10.5603/fm.a2021.0015) for the web search "sambar deer pupil shape"; the results showed no title. A morphology journal ranking first for the sambar's pupil suggests an anatomical study of the sambar eye, which would describe the pupil and may describe the tapetum. Pupil shape and the tapetum carry within a genus (rule 3). Not opened.
get: open access per the search result: https://journals.viamedica.pl/folia_morphologica/article/view/72292

title: Comparative morphology of the tapetum lucidum (among selected species)
why: Rusa: a comparative survey of the tapetum lucidum in selected mammals, listed in canon.jsonl for the tapetum (covering Artiodactyla among other orders) and already on main's canon wanted lists; it came back third for the web search "Cervus unicolor tapetum lucidum". Its species list was not visible, so it may describe the tapetum of a sambar or rusa deer. Not opened; title and address from the search result.
